precepts.text: Honour widows that are widows indeed. A widow indeed had a duty: she trusted in God and continued in supplications and prayers night and day. There was a widowhood of sisters whose job was to pray for Israel, fasting and praying night and day; she didn't just sit around because her husband died. Not under threescore years old, the wife of one man, well reported of for good works. But the younger widows refuse: when they have begun to wax wanton against Christ, they will marry, having damnation, because they have cast off their first faith; that vow was not taken lightly. Let the younger women marry, bear children, guide the house. And if any that believeth have widows in the family, let them relieve them, and let not the church be charged, so the church may relieve them that are widows indeed.
precepts.point: The high priest told him that there was such money laid up for the relief of widows and fatherless children, and that some of it belonged to Hircanus son of Tobias, a man of great dignity, and not as that wicked Simon had misinformed: in all four hundred talents of silver and two hundred of gold. And that it was altogether impossible that such wrong should be done unto them that had committed it to the holiness of the place.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
The money in the temple was “laid up for the relief of widows and fatherless children.” What is a widow? You may say, a sister whose husband died. But Paul says, “Honour widows that are widows indeed.”

First, “if any widow have children or nephews, let them learn first to shew piety at home, and to requite their parents.” Then: “Now she that is a widow indeed, and desolate, trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day.” A widow had a duty. “But she that liveth in pleasure is dead while she liveth”, because the widows made a kind of vow to dedicate themselves to the Lord and pray night and day for the benefit of Israel. And “if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel”: the family looks after her first and foremost.

“Let not a widow be taken into the number under threescore years old, having been the wife of one man.” There was a widowhood of sisters whose job was to pray for Israel, fasting and praying night and day. She didn’t just sit around and say, my husband died, I’m a widow. She had an obligation. She had to be sixty, married to one man in her life, “Well reported of for good works”: she raised children, lodged strangers, the brothers who came to the city, washed the saints’ feet, relieved the afflicted.

“But the younger widows refuse: for when they have begun to wax wanton against Christ, they will marry.” Wanton means lustful. She gave up the vow to pray and fast night and day because she wanted a man. “Having damnation, because they have cast off their first faith.” That widowhood was not taken lightly. And they learn to be idle, “wandering about from house to house”, tattlers and busybodies. So “I will therefore that the younger women marry, bear children, guide the house”: get a husband, sister.

“If any man or woman that believeth have widows, let them relieve them, and let not the church be charged; that it may relieve them that are widows indeed.” You, her son, her daughter, her uncle, her brother, take care of her, so the church can care for the real widows who have no family. That is who the money Simon betrayed was for.

precepts.text: But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel. Lord, I did not eat pork, I kept the Sabbath; but you did not take care of your wife and your kids, you left the house, you did nothing for her. That man denied the faith. Is that man going to see the kingdom? No.
precepts.point: Sisters, if you only knew: a righteous man will do almost anything to see you happy. The teaching from the teacher's own daughter: she comes running to the door, keeps her demeanor sweet, and can get anything from him; she knows her role and plays it well. If you want, you have to be a princess. Reverence him, make him feel like he is everything he is supposed to be, and watch what happens. All sisters were taught to use the physical to get what they want; a righteous man needs your spirit to be right, and then you will see that Ephesians 5 man you desperately want.

note.label: Respect: The Evidence Of Her Faith

precepts.why:
When Ephesians 5 is read, some think there's wiggle room: that doesn't really mean that. This makes complete sense on the brothers' side of the room: “But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.”

Provide means her food, her raiment, her clothing. Lord, I didn't eat pork, I didn't eat shrimp or lobster, I stopped dealing with the prostitutes, I kept the Sabbath day holy. But you didn't take care of your wife or your kids. You were a deadbeat; you did nothing for her; you left the house, living among everybody else doing what you wanted, saying, I'm not dealing with that woman no more. That was your wife. That man has denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel. Is that man going to see the kingdom? No.

“Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church”. Is that an option? If I don't do that, will I see the kingdom? The natural thing for the evil man on this side of the earth is to be promiscuous, to roam, with nothing holding him down. Is that love? No.

So what makes you think it's any different when a wife doesn't submit? Your level of faith is shown by the level of respect you have for your husband, because that is the level of respect you have for God. The same goes for the man: the way you love and care for your wife is the level of love you have for Christ. If you don't love, protect and provide for her, you're an infidel; if you don't respect your husband and do what he says, you're an infidel. Fringes and every Sabbath don't matter.

precepts.text: The elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, with all purity.
precepts.point: Come out from among them and be ye separate, and I will receive you and be a father unto you. The congregation becomes father and mother to those who come in with no parents to teach them.

note.label: Transforming From Immorality To Beautiful Civility Returning Our Kingdom To An Organized Nation Pt 3

precepts.why:
“The elder women as mothers”. The mothers out there did not teach anything. The daughters ran wild, the sons ran wild, and the daddies taught nothing. But the children heard the prophets say, come out of that. So the elder women in this truth become mothers to the sisters who come in without proper guidance. That is the importance of you elders, and why we thank the Lord for the sisters still holding on to righteousness, because Satan went after our sisters and got a lot of them messed up.

“the younger as sisters”: the younger women become sisters to the disenfranchised sisters coming in. A sister who comes in does not know how to put a skirt on, dress properly, carry herself or hold a righteous conversation. She learns from sisters who were guided by proper mothers and fathers in the body. The brothers are the same: we are a proper influence on brothers who came from total dysfunction. And it is to be done “with all purity.”

Sometimes the children get fixed up first and go back home to that sinful family. The parents notice the righteous change and ask the reason of the hope that is in them: where did you learn this respect for me, when I have been nothing but a bad father or mother to you? Then those parents come in and become repentant mothers and fathers.

This is how the Lord keeps his word, “I will receive you”, and “will be a Father unto you”. The whole nation, men and women, elder mothers and elder brothers, becomes the family we all need, and when you marry, you carry it on to your children through your generations.

precepts.text: We used to bring this out only for the dead beat who would not work. But a man who leaves everything else unfilled makes her maintain that role too, and she was never constructed for it.
precepts.point: The title of husband no more came with the understanding of it than the title of soldier, officer, captain or deacon did. You have to go through the paces.

precepts.text: The elders over the congregations, the captains and the leaders, are fathers. That is why their blessing on a union carries the same weight as the biological father's.
precepts.point: A brother dealing with erectile dysfunction has to tell the sister before he marries her. Marrying her without telling her is not just deceit, that is oppression. Talk to her and work on it together. And adultery is adultery no matter how you look at it: his condition does not cosign a wife stepping outside of her marriage.

precepts.text: Provide for thine own and specially for those of thine own house; the own is the nation, the house is the family.
precepts.point: Charge them that are rich that they be not highminded, but ready to distribute, willing to communicate. Most of us today have no fields or vineyards, but some have good jobs and blessed incomes; you cannot take it with you, so give of your substance. The scriptures also say no good can come to him that gives no alms.

note.label: Leviticus 19: Ye Shall Be Holy, for I the Lord Your God Am Holy

precepts.why:
The corners of the field, the gleanings of the harvest and the leavings of the vineyard belonged to the poor and the stranger. The Most High is teaching, do not be selfish: love thy neighbour as thyself and look out for the poor of your people.

“if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.” Those of his own house are his wife and children; his own is his nation. Care for your people, as the law of the gleanings taught.

precepts.text: The elders that labour in the word and doctrine are worthy of double honour, for thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn.
precepts.point: Giving double honour is not just saying the words to the leadership; it is true respect and reverence toward the leadership that labours in this word and doctrine.

note.label: Deuteronomy 25: Just Judgment, the Brother's Duty, and Amalek

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not muzzle the ox when he treadeth out the corn”: the corn is the reward for the ox. Paul applies this verse to how the elders are treated: “Let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine. For the scripture saith, Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn. And, The labourer is worthy of his reward.”

The ox that treads out the corn is not kept from it; the elder that labours in the word and doctrine is worthy of his reward, double honour. Giving double honour is not just saying the words to the leadership; it is true respect and reverence toward the leadership that labours in this word and doctrine.

precepts.text: Providing for your own house is where leaving an inheritance begins; first you have to work.
precepts.point: The Lord grant you that ye may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband: that rest is an inheritance. The man is supposed to leave an inheritance; you are not supposed to leave your wife and your children desolate with a gang of bills. To leave an inheritance you first have to work, and you have to be wise with how you deal with your money.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
Leaving an inheritance begins with providing for your own house. “But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.”

To leave an inheritance you first have to work, and you have to be wise with how you deal with your money. Some of us use captivity as an excuse not to better ourselves or build, but that is not what the scriptures say: get the job, further your education, do more for yourself, your family and the body. A man who does not provide for his own has denied the faith.

precepts.text: In Israel the younger widows are refused, for when they begin to wax wanton against Christ they will marry; a young widow still has years to bear children and that urge will most likely come upon her, which is why Naomi released them.
precepts.point: Naomi was free of her responsibility toward them: her husband had died, her sons their husbands had died, and their husbands had left them inheritances in Moab. She would not put them under an oath to stay and wait for sons that would likely never come.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
Naomi would not hold her daughters in law to wait for sons that would likely never come. In Israel the same thing is understood of young widows: “But the younger widows refuse: for when they have begun to wax wanton against Christ, they will marry”.

A young widow still has years to bear children, and that urge will most likely come upon her; she is not going to wait. Orpah and Ruth were grown women, and Naomi was free of her responsibility toward them: her husband had died, her sons their husbands had died, and their husbands had left them inheritances in Moab. So she would not put them under an oath to stay, and released them.

precepts.text: He that provides not for his own house hath denied the faith and is worse than an infidel, so do not hang around a slothful man or woman.
precepts.point: The mischief framed by law is men marrying men, women marrying women, setting the new year in the midst of winter to have us worshiping another god, and coexist meaning you can serve any gods you want.

note.label: Psalm 94: The God of Vengeance and Defense of His People

precepts.why:
Paul asks what part he that believeth has with an infidel, and then shows who the infidel is among us: “But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.”

He that provides not for his own house has denied the faith and is worse than an infidel. So do not hang around a slothful man or woman. The throne of iniquity that frames mischief by a law has no fellowship with the Most High, and the one who will not provide for his own house is worse than the unbeliever we are told not to be yoked with.

precepts.text: The man who provides not for his own house has denied the faith and is worse than an infidel.
precepts.point: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands, and poverty comes as one that travels and want as an armed man. This is why in the proving stage the sisters and leadership ask a brother whether he works, has his own place, and can provide for a woman and offspring. Leadership keeps a report on these men so there are no back-door marriages.

note.label: Proverbs 6: The Surety, the Sluggard, and the Six Things the Most High Hates

precepts.why:
“Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep: So shall thy poverty come as one that travelleth, and thy want as an armed man.” The ant, with no guide, overseer or ruler, provides her meat in the summer and gathers her food in the harvest; the sluggard folds his hands and poverty comes.

Paul says what that means for a man with a house: “But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.” The man who provides not for his own house has denied the faith and is worse than an infidel.

This is why in the proving stage the sisters and leadership ask a brother whether he works, has his own place, and can provide for a woman and offspring. Leadership keeps a report on these men so there are no back-door marriages. A sluggard cannot provide for his own, and a man who cannot provide has denied the faith.

precepts.text: The widow taken into the number must be sixty, the wife of one man, and well reported of for good works, before the younger widows are refused.
precepts.point: Paul sets the age at sixty because younger widows still have fleshly desires and will begin to wax wanton against Christ and want to marry, turning their focus off the work. A woman whose desire is toward the ministry and who has a pattern of good works is worthy to be taken care of; one still looking for a husband should marry and be provided for by a husband.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
The daily ministration to the widows had a criterion. “Let not a widow be taken into the number under threescore years old, having been the wife of one man, Well reported of for good works; if she have brought up children, if she have lodged strangers, if she have washed the saints’ feet, if she have relieved the afflicted, if she have diligently followed every good work.”

The widow taken into the number must be sixty, the wife of one man, and well reported of for good works. “But the younger widows refuse: for when they have begun to wax wanton against Christ, they will marry; Having damnation, because they have cast off their first faith.” That is the order behind the ministration the Grecian widows were neglected in.

points: I will therefore that the younger women marry, bear children, guide the house, give none occasion to the adversary to speak reproachfully. Why was Paul addressing the younger women marrying? The younger widows were looking to the church to fund their lives. The answer was: you younger women, marry, so you can be taken care of by your husband. The school helps the older widows, and the active widows; but you younger women are expected to move on and marry.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

points: Another sister asked how to encourage her lord to spend time with the girls in a blended family. Answer: stop trying to tell a man how to be a father; that is that bossy spirit trying to find an excuse to instruct him. Influence him through your own actions: take the girls to the park yourself and let your example provoke him. Complaining and nagging has never moved a man; pray to the Most High and be a good influence. And sisters, be honest about the choices that created the blended situation; we are not miracle workers.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

points: Problems come in our households because we keep score: I provide, I pay all the bills, I take care of this and that. But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel. You are supposed to do that. That is your reasonable service, a commandment of God. Congratulations for doing your job. You cannot throw in your wife's face that you do what you are supposed to do.

note.label: This Woman's Work

points: What is the opposite of the eunuch for the women? The widow. A lot of times when people read about widows they think it is just a woman whose husband died, but it was much more than that. There are two types: a sister whose husband died, and a woman who makes a vow to serve God, to fast and pray, and to help the brothers and sisters in the body. Judith was young when her husband died, and she said, I will dedicate my life to the Lord; she was fasting most of the week, and she made a vow to God not to marry again. The same way some men became eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven's sake, some women made a vow to follow the Lord and not deal with a man, for the kingdom's sake.

But the younger widows refuse: when they have begun to wax wanton against Christ, they will marry, having damnation, because they have cast off their first faith. Is it wrong for them to get married? No; the damnation comes because they took the vow of widowhood, they made a vow to control their desires and serve God, and they broke that vow. So Paul said refuse the young women that come around saying they want to be widows, because they are going to bring condemnation on themselves.

note.label: Sexual Discipline

points: This is talking about the younger widows. They learn to be idle, wandering about from house to house; and not only idle, but tattlers also and busybodies, speaking things which they ought not.

Brothers, you don't need to know everything. Some of you have been privileged to sit amongst leadership; you might be in the backyard and overhear a conversation. You would be a complete and utter idiot to utter anything you've heard, especially because it wasn't spoken to you; you just happened to be a fly on the wall. When leaders discuss certain things, we are coming to a solution to deal with it. If you're not dealing with it, you don't need the information.

Sisters, same thing. There's elder sisters and senior sisters that counsel, so certain information gets filtered, and they do discuss with each other because they're counseling to figure out how to help a person. That doesn't open up the door for you to think, oh, this is what we do, we're going to talk about sister so-and-so. There is a need-to-know basis.

I say this from a perspective for y'all: before I became a deacon, I didn't know anything, and Israel was so beautiful. Everything was so grand. You in the spirit: man, Christ going to come back any day now, we in this together. Then you get into a seat of leadership, and you find out about all the problems. Now things ain't so beautiful; the room got a lot darker. And I'm telling you, it was far better before you knew.

Stay in the place of not needing to know. I'm a deacon, and there's things that I don't ask about, cuz I don't want to know unless I have to know. There's things in other regions that I ain't got to be privy on, and I'm okay with that, cuz they got a whole deacon over there that's dealing with it. I trust he's handling his job. It's none of my business. Stop being so nosy. Leave it be.

Video played: nosy people may quickly say that they're your friend, or that they're trying to help you, or that you're being ungrateful. But really, they're just trying to protect their access to your life. Beware of them. Some people do it for alliance.

To be an example to the men, to the women, and especially to the young men. The bishop has been in this truth over twenty years, putting his brick in, longer than some of you have been alive; do you think we are going to allow you to come in here and disrespect these men? That is not going to happen. You might as well go back to that church.

One thing I hate is disrespect. The same way I will not allow young men to disrespect the officers, I will not allow you to disrespect the officer next to you. We come from a society where it is okay to disrespect the black man; we cannot allow that here. If you are that person, we will give you a warning, maybe two, and after that you have to go, especially when it comes to our elders.

note.label: Why Do Fools Fall In Love

The title of husband no more came with the understanding of it than the title of soldier, officer, captain or deacon did. You have to go through the paces.
